thesis: Okta disclosed fiscal-Q2 revenue growth of 11%, subscription growth of 12%, current remaining performance obligations growth of 14%, GAAP operating margin of 13% versus 6% a year earlier, and non-GAAP free cash flow of $227 million. This suggests improving backlog and operating leverage support a long thesis. The strongest counter-evidence is full-year revenue guidance of only 10% to 11% growth and fiscal-Q3 non-GAAP operating-margin guidance of 24% to 25% versus 28% in fiscal Q2; accelerating current RPO, the higher GAAP margin, and improved free-cash-flow margin outweigh that near-term moderation. The latest available Form 10-Q reported no material legal matters, and targeted checks found no qualifying scheduled litigation step or completed three-year governance event.
invalidation: Current RPO growth reverses materially, GAAP operating margin falls back toward the prior-year level, or a material security or legal event undermines customer retention before the next review.

thesis: Veeva disclosed fiscal-Q2 revenue growth of 18%, subscription growth of 16%, GAAP operating-income growth of 40%, and an improved full-year outlook, while Vault CRM reached more than 180 live customers and 12 top-20-biopharma commitments. This suggests broad product adoption and operating leverage support a long thesis. The strongest counter-evidence is that fiscal-Q3 revenue guidance of $932 million to $935 million is only modestly above fiscal-Q2 revenue of $928 million, while CRM migration and customer concentration remain execution risks; that does not change the read because the confirmed quarter exceeded company guidance across metrics, commitments broadened, and GAAP operating income grew faster than revenue. The latest available Form 10-Q reported no material legal proceedings, and targeted checks found no qualifying scheduled litigation step or completed three-year governance event.
invalidation: The company cuts its full-year revenue or non-GAAP operating-income outlook, Vault CRM loses major customer commitments, or GAAP operating-income growth falls below revenue growth without a one-time explanation.

thesis: Hyperliquid Strategies disclosed fiscal-year net income of $305.5 million, but $709.9 million of that result came from unrealized HYPE-token gains before a one-time token contribution loss and deferred tax expense. The company also disclosed raising $646.6 million through a committed equity facility at an average issue price of $8.70 per share while using the proceeds principally to accumulate HYPE. This suggests the equity remains a volatile token proxy whose reported profit and per-share economics depend on HYPE prices and continuing share issuance, so the mixed evidence supports avoiding a new position. The strongest counter-evidence is $132.6 million of cash as of August 19, zero debt, and 29.3 million HYPE tokens; those balance-sheet positives do not resolve the dilution and mark-to-market dependence. A July SEC filing said earlier going-concern doubt had been alleviated by capital raising, disclosed only ordinary-course legal matters, and targeted checks found no qualifying scheduled litigation step or completed three-year governance event.
invalidation: Reconsider the avoid thesis only if the company demonstrates sustained per-share HYPE and cash growth without material new issuance and recurring operating or staking income becomes substantial relative to token mark-to-market changes.
